item: The persisted rollup refresh compares the library generation before it merges, so a corpus swap during it cannot add a tail read from the new file to a store built from the old one
refs: R303 limit; follow-on of #1551; PR pending
summary: #1551 left refresh_keyword_daily (the persisted store's maintainer) without a hook. It now takes the build's on_batch(stage, rows_done): after every batch of the mention tail and once before the merge begins; the persisted dispatcher path passes the stamp comparison (library_generation.current() read before the session reads a row, compared with the guard's own valid(), never waiting) and compares once more before the store is recorded as serving. The full path passes the hook to build_keyword_daily. The stop is made BEFORE the merge because the merge (UPDATE, INSERT, then the watermark) is not transactional: a stop between the first statement and the watermark would be added twice by the next refresh; a raise drops the stage table and propagates as StaleLibraryError, which #1547's branch turns into no hold and a retry. Tests do a real swap on a guarded engine and the real refresh over an in-memory store: nothing merged, watermark unmoved, stage table gone, the retry equals a full rebuild; each of six mutants (no mentions hook, no aggregate hook, no stage drop, full path without the hook, no final compare, hook not passed) fails its own case. LIMITS: a swap between the pre-merge comparison and the watermark write (the merge itself, DuckDB-only and not interruptible) lands a store with the old corpus's days and the new file's tail, which the next refresh repairs only if the corpus epoch differs (a restore of an equal-epoch backup does not); a window that is then refused before it touches anything stops the refresh once, as #1551 states; Windows handles not measured.
